Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz to open for Afghanistan. Taskin Ahmed to bowl first.
... The Run Chase ...

With the pitch expected to slow down further, Bangladesh's spinners might play a key role in the chase. The match is evenly poised, and the outcome will depend on how both teams adapt to the changing conditions. The stage is set for an exciting chase, with Afghanistan looking to overcome the 222-run target. Will their spinners continue to dominate, or will Bangladesh's bowlers find a way to restrict them? Lets find out with the chase in a while.

Afghanistan's bowlers were impressive throughout, with Azmatullah Omarzai shining with the new ball, taking 3 wickets. The spin trio of Nangeyalia Kharote, Rashid Khan, and AM Ghazanfar also bowled effectively, with Rashid Khan standing out, claiming 3 wickets. AM Ghazanfar took a couple and Kharote took one wicket as well.

Bangladesh's innings got off to a rocky start, but a crucial partnership between Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Tawhid Hridoy helped them post a fighting total. The duo added 101 runs for the 4th wicket, with both players scoring half-centuries before getting dismissed. Their partnership helped Bangladesh post a competitive total of 221 runs. Saif Hassan also looked promising, getting a start before being dismissed while trying to accelerate.

The match is indeed evenly poised with Bangladesh posting a competitive total of 221 runs, thanks to significant contributions from Tawhid Hridoy and captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who both scored half-centuries.

The Tigers come into the 50-over leg with the wind in their sails, having whitewashed the Afghans 3-0 in the preceding T20I series. However, the longer format presents a different challenge, demanding greater application from the batters and allowing Afghanistan's formidable spin quartet more time to weave their magic, making this opener a crucial tone-setter. Afghanistan, recovering from the T20I clean sweep, will be desperate to put a stop to the Bangladesh juggernaut and return to winning ways in a format where they have shown resilience in the past. Led by the steady hand of Hashmatullah Shahidi, the onus will be on the likes of Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz to lay a solid foundation against a diverse Bangladesh attack. The pitches in Abu Dhabi tend to start true for the bat before slowing down, which perfectly suits the wrist-spin wizardry of Rashid Khan and the off-breaks of Mohammad Nabi, who will look to tie down the middle overs and hunt for wickets. Bangladesh, helmed by Mehidy Hasan Miraz, appear well-rounded with key performers like Towhid Hridoy and Jaker Ali showing recent form with the bat, while the pace attack spearheaded by Taskin Ahmed and the variety offered by Rishad Hossain's leg-spin have given them penetration across formats. Bangladesh's momentum and slightly superior all-round balance will face a stern test against Afghanistan's home advantage and world-class spin attack.
